newsitem.title: USA: Intraday CSCE world sugar off, nearby switch grows.
newsitem.headline: Intraday CSCE world sugar off, nearby switch grows.

text.p: The nearby switch continued to weaken as speculators rolled out of July contracts ahead of expiry, pushing prices sharply down by midday Friday, traders said.
The most-active October contract was also trading lower with at 0.22 cent premium over July as of 1133 EDT, compared with 0.14 cent on Thursday's close.
The July contract expires on Monday.
Speculative selling in the switch pressured October and triggered stops below 10.22 cents, pushing the benchmark contract to the day's low of 11.14, traders said.
They added that prices are likely to weaken further, with nearby support pegged at 11.00 cents, followed by the recent low of 10.96 cents in October.
At least one sugar broker said the contract could fall to 10.80 cents over the next few days, while July also continues to wither amid a lack of buying.
Open interest in July remained at 17,353 lots, down 6,744 lots, as of Thursday. October's liquidity fell by 38 lots to stand at 91,398 lots.
Volume was estimated at a brisk 18,339 contracts, as of 1100 EDT.

As of 1133 EDT, the July contract was down 0.17 cent at 10.94 cents per lb, traded 11.13 to 10.92 cents. October stood 0.09 cent lower at 11.16 cents, while the rest of the board was down 0.07 to 0.11 cent.
Technical resistance in October remained at 11.34 cents, followed by 11.42 cents in October.
